meghiya.notes: AN 9.3 and Ud 4.1 identify the attendant who asked to meditate in the mango grove. Thag 1.66 attributes the attainment of the three knowledges to Meghiya. Neither discourse dates his awakening to the end of the conversation. AN 9.2 is an adjacent discourse.

metteyya.notes: DN 26 foretells the Buddha of this name. Metteyya 02 describes the elder who asks about sexual intercourse in Snp 4.7. The closing list in Snp 4.16 names that discourse between Jarā and Pasūra. The young brahmin sense fits Bāvarī’s pupil in Snp 5.3, whose question AN 6.61 quotes under the compound metteyyapañhe. DPPN treats the pupil separately under Tissa 9. The shared name supplies no basis for assigning the elder’s entry to the pupil.

meṇḍasira.notes: Thag 1.78 attributes the verse to Meṇḍasira. Thag 1.80 repeats his name in the chapter’s closing list.

migapathaka.notes: Citta visits Migapathaka on business in SN 41.1. The page also covers SN 40.11, a conversation with deities.

migasālā.notes: In AN 6.44 and AN 10.75 the laywoman asks Ānanda about her father Purāṇa and her uncle Isidatta. AN 6.43 and AN 10.74 are neighboring discourses. AN 10.80 repeats her name in the chapter’s closing list.

migāra.notes: Ugga calls the wealthy man Migāra Rohaṇeyya in AN 7.7. AN 7.8 and AN 7.9 discuss other subjects. DPD’s MN 107 example names the longhouse of Migāra’s mother in a compound and gives no grounds for identifying that Migāra as Rohaṇeyya.

migāramātupāsāda.notes: AN 3.66, SN 3.11, Ud 2.9 and Ud 6.2 name the longhouse in the Eastern Monastery at Sāvatthī. The neighboring AN 3.65 and SN 3.10 lack this setting.

missakā.notes: DN 20 at 17.6 lists missakā ca yasassino among the assembled deities. Sujato renders the words as ‘and assorted glorious ones’, which accounts for the packet’s zero mentions.

mithilā.notes: DN 19 pairs Mithilā with the Videhas. MN 83 and MN 91 name the city, as does Vāseṭṭhī in Thig 6.2. The page references also pick up MN 82 and MN 90, where the place names are Thullakoṭṭhika and Ujuññā respectively.

moggalla.notes: AN 4.187 names Moggalla among King Eḷeyya’s men who honor Rāmaputta. The citation points to AN 4.191 and AN 4.192, which cover different subjects. The packet also counts moggallāna when a monk is being addressed, as in AN 4.167. The English name Moggallāna passes the prefix check for Moggalla.

moliyasīvaka.notes: SN 36.21 and AN 6.47 both introduce Moḷiyasīvaka as a wanderer. AN 6.46 is Mahācunda’s discourse.

mucalinda.notes: DN 32 lists Mucalinda among the yakkha chiefs. Mucalinda 02 opens with the tree but also explicitly names the nāga king and recounts his sheltering the Buddha with seven coils, exactly the episode in Ud 2.1. The tree has its own compound at Ud 2.1:1.2, mucalindamūle. The lake in Mucalinda 04 has no attestation in the app’s suttas. Its citation lands in DN 8, which opens in the deer park at Kaṇṇakatthala. Claude: Mucalinda 02 is the tree's entry, so it ships among others rather than under the dragon king's sense, and Ud 2.1 has no pick.

muttā.notes: Muttā 03 is the laywoman in AN 8.91–117. AN 8.89 and AN 8.90 fall on the same page. Neither nun has a candidate here. Thig 1.2 identifies the trainee whom the Buddha addresses, and Thig 1.11 attributes the verse about freedom from mortar, pestle and husband to the elder Muttā.

māhissati.notes: Snp 5.1 includes Purimāhissatiṁ on the students’ route. DN 19 at 36.5 gives the Avanti city as Mahesayaṁ in the app’s Pāli and Māhissatī in Sujato’s translation. The spelling accounts for the missing DN 19 mention.

mānadinna.notes: In SN 47.30 the sick householder tells Ānanda about his mindfulness practice and the five lower fetters. SN 47.31 begins a new chapter.

mānatthaddha.notes: MN 116 lists the privately awakened Buddha. SN 7.15:1.2 explicitly calls the brahmin mānatthaddho nāma brāhmaṇo. Sujato calls him ‘Stuck-Up’, so the packet misses the very discourse that settles Mānatthaddha 01. SN 7.14 and MN 117 are adjacent page matches.

mātaṅga.notes: MN 116 lists the privately awakened Buddha. MN 56 names the forest in the compound mātaṅgāraññaṁ. Snp 1.7 describes a corpse-worker’s son named Mātaṅga who was reborn in the Brahmā world. Neither the forest nor this man has an entry in the packet.

māyā.notes: DN 14 and Thig 6.6 name Gotama’s mother. Thag 10.1:8.2 also names her in the compound māyanāmā, which has its own dictionary line. The verses there describe her rejoicing in heaven. The detail about rebirth as a male deity comes from the dictionary’s further account.

māṇavagāmiya.notes: SN 2.30 names the six visiting gods and identifies Māṇavagāmiya as the one who praises the Buddha. SN 2.29 concerns Susīma.

nagaraka.notes: MN 89 traces Pasenadi’s journey from Nagaraka to Medaḷumpa. MN 121, SN 3.18 and SN 45.2 call Nagaraka a Sakyan town. Sujato translates its name as ‘Townsville’.

nagaravinda.notes: MN 150 opens in this Kosalan brahmin village. The page also covers the end of MN 149.

nala.notes: DN 32:10.9 names Naḷa beside Janesabha as naḷo rājā, repeated at 12.258. The English spelling ‘Nala’ misses the filter for ‘Naḷa’. DN 20:10.10 has the same pairing in the form naḷorājā, which DPD treats as its own headword.

nalakapāna.notes: MN 68 and AN 10.67–68 place the Buddha in the Palāsa grove at Naḷakapāna. AN 10.70 names the pair of discourses in its closing list. MN 67 and AN 10.66 are neighboring page matches.

nanda.notes: AN 1.230 and AN 8.9 identify the monk by his sense restraint, SN 21.8 and Ud 3.2 by kinship, and Thag 2.19 by his ornamentation and the Buddha’s help. The closing list at Thag 2.20:3.5 repeats his name outside the packet. Ud 3.2:10.2 promises five hundred nymphs, where Nanda 01 says one. Ud 1.5 gives only a list of elders. Nanda Vaccha (AN 6.57, MN 36, MN 76) and Veḷukaṇṭakī’s son (AN 7.53) lack candidates. Nanda 02 is Bāvarī’s student, and Thag 1.36 names Nanda 19 as Kumāputta. AN 1.240, DN 16 and SN 55.8 refer to nuns named Nandā. MN 116:6.23 gives twelve across three names without specifying how many bore each. The other page matches AN 1.248–257, AN 8.8, SN 21.9, SN 35.242 and SN 2.26 lack the corresponding Nanda episodes.
